title: ChatCRM
deck: A shared WhatsApp inbox where every conversation is assigned to an agent and becomes a customer you can measure.

blocks.text: Many companies serve customers over WhatsApp from a single phone. Nobody knows who answered, how long it took or whether the customer was happy; as the team grows, messages get lost.
The goal: every phone number becomes a customer with history, every conversation has an owner, and the team sees its metrics in real time.

I am the main author of the API (NestJS) and the web app (React), with more than 1,000 commits. I designed the three-service architecture, the shared contracts and the security layer; I integrated the AI service as an optional dependency.
Three decoupled services. The API is the only one that talks to Meta; the app only knows the API, and the AI service can be switched off without breaking anything.

blocks.caption: Fig. 2 — An inbound message: Meta gets its 200 before the slow work runs.

blocks.text: **1. Signature verified per channel, not globally.** One endpoint receives webhooks for several companies. Accepting a signature from *any* channel would let the owner of one Meta app inject events into another company's channel, so every channel the payload mentions must validate with *its own* secrets, in constant time.

blocks.caption: HMAC-SHA256 over the raw bytes and constant-time comparison.

blocks.text: **2. Credentials encrypted at rest.** Each company's WhatsApp tokens are stored with AES-256-GCM inside a versioned JSON envelope (`v`, `iv`, `authTag`, `ciphertext`), so the algorithm can be rotated without a schema migration.

blocks.caption: Versioned envelope: the key comes from CREDENTIALS_ENCRYPTION_KEY and is checked to be 32 bytes.

blocks.text: **3. One contract, three uses.** The Zod schemas in `src/contracts/` validate requests, serialise responses, generate the OpenAPI docs and are imported by the web app. A contract change breaks the build on both sides instead of failing in production.

**4. Slow work goes to queues.** Meta retries when the webhook is slow. The API returns 200 as soon as the message is stored; downloading media and scoring sentiment run on BullMQ queues with their own retries.
The `chat-crm-ia` service uses pysentimiento, a transformer trained for Spanish. It receives a message and returns its label with probabilities; the API stores the result and feeds the dashboard.

items: Real-time shared inbox with automatic conversation assignment.
Dashboard with monthly KPIs, trends, agent ranking and sentiment.
First-run setup in a single transaction: admin, company and WhatsApp channel.

quote: A shared contract breaks the build; a duplicated type breaks production.
